metadata.title: Claude, K12 Lesson Planning.
metadata.subtitle: A List, Not a Freshly-Reasoned Plan
metadata.purpose: Take a Claude skill apart in the Teardown register: when Claude plans a K-12 lesson, it isn't reasoning the plan fresh — it's running the k12-lesson-planning skill's written steps out of SKILL.md, backed by a references folder of source material and a scripts folder of runnable code. Name the trade-off: they optimized for repeatability at the expense of coverage — anything the list doesn't cover falls back to Claude's own judgment, not the skill's playbook.

beats.narration_text: Liam here, in for Bear. You'd guess Claude improvises a lesson plan — reads the topic, freestyles a syllabus. It doesn't. Ask it to plan a K-12 lesson and it opens a written file first, then runs the list. Here's what's actually happening under the hood.

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. triggerWords/replacementWords must be a SINGLE whitespace token each (the component matches trigger against one split token's punctuation-stripped core; a multi-word trigger never matches and the correction silently never fires — confirmed as a defect on the k12-lesson-differentiation sibling built earlier this batch) and the trigger should be the LAST content word before terminal punctuation so nothing trails the replacement ungrammatically. 'improvise' is a single token immediately before the terminal '?', so this reel does not repeat that defect. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('improvise' -> 'follow written steps') lands on screen.

beats.narration_text: Take a Claude skill apart, and here's what you find. It's a folder — Claude reads it before it acts. This one is called k12-lesson-planning. Inside: a SKILL.md file, in plain language, no hidden logic, no secret sauce. The file is the program.

Here's the mechanism, in full. Inside SKILL.md sits a Steps section — a numbered list Claude runs top to bottom. Read a step, execute it, return the result, next step. No branching, unless a step itself says to branch.

production_viz.label: READ, EXECUTE, RETURN
production_viz.caption: linear — no branching unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: Here's what's different about this particular skill: it isn't only prose. Alongside SKILL.md, the folder ships two more things — a references folder of source material, and a scripts folder of runnable code. Where a step can run as code, it does. That's what they optimized for: the same input, the same output, every run — not a freshly-reasoned answer typed out each time.

production_viz.label: NOT ONLY PROSE
production_viz.caption: code where it can — not reasoned fresh each time

beats.narration_text: Claude isn't improvising the lesson plan. It's running the k12-lesson-planning skill's written list of steps, in order — repeatable to a fault. Ask for something the list doesn't cover, and you get Claude's own judgment, not the skill's playbook.

props.quote: Claude isn't improvising the lesson plan. It's running the k12-lesson-planning skill's written list of steps, in order — repeatable to a fault. Ask for something the list doesn't cover, and you get Claude's own judgment, not the skill's playbook.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: ask it to write a short SKILL.md for a K12-LESSON-PLANNING skill — three to five numbered steps that turn a grade level, a subject, and a topic into a complete lesson plan with objectives, activities, and an assessment. Then run it twice on the same inputs and check the two plans come out the same shape. Then run it on a case the list clearly doesn't cover — say, a mixed-grade special-education class — and watch exactly where it stops. Go deeper: add a sixth step that says 'use your judgment on prerequisites,' and see whether the list still behaves like a list, or has just handed the whole decision back to the model.

llm_exercise.prompt: I want to understand how Claude runs a written skill. A Claude 'skill' is a folder holding SKILL.md — a numbered list of steps Claude reads and runs top to bottom, with no judgment step. Write me a short SKILL.md for a K12-LESSON-PLANNING skill: three to five numbered steps that turn a grade level, subject, and topic into a complete lesson plan (objectives, activities, assessment). Then run it twice on the same inputs (grade 7, science, water cycle) and show the two outputs come out the same shape. Then run it on a case the list clearly doesn't cover — a mixed-grade special-education class studying the water cycle — and show me exactly where it stops.
